title: Ask Shearwater: compact signal almanac & engineering hooks
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note gathers a compact set of recurring customer asks we observed in the last six weeks across Solutions, CS field notes, and incoming support tickets. Goal: turn raw asks into a small set of engineering hooks and low-effort probes (Shearwater probes) we can run in Q2 to validate impact on cost and latency without heavy infra changes.

Sources and signal weight:
- CS triage board (Apr 2026) — 18 tickets flagged as KV-cache or cold-start related; top accounts: AcmeHealth, LexiSearch, MapFoundry.
- Solutions onboarding interviews (3 customers) — qualitative heat on: rollout safety, quantization variance, visibility into per-request cost.
- Support thread sampling (15 threads) — frequent asks: 'why token cost spikes', 'fallback model mismatch', 'inconsistent latency at scale'.

Core customer needs (synthesized):
1) Predictable per-request economics: customers want a simple knob or preview that shows expected per-call token cost and latency percentile before they deploy a new prompt/model combo.
2) Lightweight per-route caching controls: product teams want TTL and prefix-match control on a per-route level (not only on global model level) to tune conversational apps.
3) Graceful fallback visibility: when Redwood routes to a cheaper/quantized variant, customers want clear attribution + A/B tracing to ensure quality regressions are detectable.
4) Faster cold-starts for small bursty customers: micro‑warm pools or instant KV prime suggested.
5) Rollout circuit-breakers: automatic rollback when quality metrics (from eval sets) cross a threshold.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim-ish):
- "We love the dedicated pools but sometimes we get latency spikes mid-day. Hard to explain to product managers." — Customer A (SaaS startup).
- "If a fallback model kicks in we can’t tell if text quality changed — need a trace back to the variant and a quick eval snapshot." — Customer B (fintech).

Shearwater probes (low-effort experiments):
A. Per-request cost preview (UI + lightweight backend probe)
 - Idea: expose an API /preview that returns estimated token usage/latency p50/p95 given prompt length and model variant. Back-of-envelope implementation: run sampled tokenization + cached speed profile lookup for the model/seq-length band.
 - Engineering hook: small microservice that reads existing model perf profiles and tokenizes client prompt. Return is memoizable for identical prompts.
 - Success metric: 80% of previewed calls within ±15% of real cost during 7-day sample.
 - Estimated dev effort: 1.5 engineer-weeks + 1 FE day.

B. Route-level prefix cache controls (feature-flagged)
 - Idea: allow route configs: {prefix_ttl, prefix_match_mode} with modes: exact | prefix | fuzzy. Implement as a policy layer consult before runtime cache lookup.
 - Engineering hook: leverage existing KV cache sharding; add a config read in request routing. Ship behind FF for 10 beta customers.
 - Success metric: per-route cost drop >= 20% for at least 4 beta customers without p95 latency regressions.
 - Estimated dev effort: 2 engineer-weeks + ops config changes.

C. Fallback attribution tracer
 - Idea: when smart-routing picks a variant, attach metadata in response header + log event linking request_id -> variant_id -> perf_delta. Provide a simple UI view (console) that surfaces when a fallback occurred and sample outputs side-by-side.
 - Engineering hook: enrich existing routing trace events and add a small console card in Debug view.
 - Success metric: CS can diagnose fallback-driven quality complaints in <10m in 80% of cases.
 - Estimated dev effort: 1 engineer-week + 1 UX day.

D. Micro-warm primers for bursty tenants
 - Idea: allow a tenant to pre-warm KV cache for a small set of prefixes with a cost cap; background job primes instances in scale zone.
 - Engineering hook: reuse warm pool infra; add tenant-level warm request generator and accounting.
 - Success metric: reduce cold-start p99 by 30% for targeted workloads.
 - Estimated dev effort: 3 engineer-weeks + perf testing.

Prioritization (heuristic):
- Quick wins: C (fallback tracer) and A (preview) — high CS value, low infra risk.
- Medium: B (prefix controls) — moderate infra changes but direct cost savings.
- Heavy: D (micro-warms) — higher infra/ops complexity; pilot with 2 customers only.

Quality and risk notes:
- Any preview/cost estimation must clearly state "estimate" to avoid billing disputes. Consider non-binding previews.
- Prefix-cache modes must preserve privacy: do not leak keys between tenants; ensure tenant-scoped keys.
- Warm primer needs throttles to avoid gaming (customer pre-warm to monopolize pools). Enforce per-tenant caps.

Measurement plan and telemetry hooks:
- Add a small set of telemetry counters: preview_requests, preview_accuracy_band, route_prefix_savings, fallback_incidents, warm_prime_success. Track by customer, route, and model.
- Create a dashboard (Optimize Console) with 7/30-day windows for these metrics and an export CSV.

Suggested owners and next steps (this sprint):
- Aisha P. (Product) — owner for overall probe coordination and CS beta recruitment.
- Miguel R. (Eng) — lead for Probe A + C.
- Claire H. (Eng/Product) — route config prototype and FF gating (Probe B).
- Evan B. (SRE) — measurement and dashboard plumbing.

Next actions (this week):
1) Sync with CS on 6 candidate beta customers and capture one sample prompt per customer (to seed preview model). — Owner: Aisha.
2) Create FF design doc for route-level prefix controls with API sketch and security considerations. — Owner: Claire.
3) Small spike: Miguel to implement a preview microservice skeleton and run it locally against 3 models. Target PoC by 2026-05-06.
4) Evan to define telemetry event schema and minimal dashboard wireframe.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Billing implications: are previews discoverable as meterable actions? We should flag previews as non-billable until policy decided.
- How to surface fallback rating to end-users without confusing product UX? Need experiment designs with two partner customers.
- Is per-route cache control sufficient vs. per-call dynamic suggestions (Optimize could recommend TTLs automatically)?

Notes to self / rough links:
- Related: confluence:optimize/cache-guidelines (linked)
- Prior ticket: JIRA-OPS-3189 (warm-pool incident analysis)
- Quick-wins checklist: implement C in 2 sprints; spin up preview PoC parallel.

Appendix: short example of /preview API payload + response (informal)
- Request: {"model":"rw-14b-q4", "prompt":"<user prompt...>", "max_tokens":256} 
- Response: {"estimated_tokens":142, "p50_latency_ms":78, "p95_latency_ms":210, "confidence_band":"±12%"} 

End of note.
